datasets: data/311_requests.csv (synthetic, generated by internal/seed/generator.go; labeled as 311 Service Requests)
data/vacant_buildings.csv (synthetic, generated by internal/seed/generator.go; labeled as Vacant Building Notices)
build_error: go build ./... succeeds; documented ./run.sh fails: './run.sh: line 3: syntax error near unexpected token (' because README text and a PowerShell here-string marker @' were pasted above the shebang
concurrency_primitives: Two datasets loaded in parallel goroutines + WaitGroup (main.go:45-54); per-file reader goroutine -> buffered chan of sync.Pool'd row slices -> N parser goroutines with private batches -> outCh merge (ingest/parser.go:83-127, 198-242); spatial join sharded over workers with local match slices (engine/join.go:81-143); 3 goroutines for spatial join + two GroupBys; 5 analysis goroutines (engine/analyzer.go:76-93, 177-355)
design_patterns: Builder (EngineBuilder.WithWorkers/WithHighVacancyThreshold/WithSpatialStrategy/Build), Strategy (SpatialJoinStrategy interface, HaversineGridJoin), generic functional helpers Filter/MapSlice/Fold/GroupBy; ingest->engine->render package separation
questions: Which neighborhoods have the highest concentration of sanitation/illegal-dumping 311 requests relative to registered vacant structures?
How does mean 311 resolution time compare between high-vacancy and low-vacancy neighborhoods across city agencies?
Which street/infrastructure hazards (potholes, streetlights, sidewalks) occur within 150 m of vacant buildings (haversine join)?
How should capital remediation funds be weighted across City Council districts by combined vacant count and open 311 backlog?
Does reliance on phone vs mobile-app 311 reporting shift across neighborhood vacancy tiers, and how does it relate to closure rates?
overview: A multi-package Go program (cmd, internal/seed, ingest, engine, model, render) that loads two CSVs through channel-based worker pools with sync.Pool'd buffers, runs a grid-indexed haversine spatial join and two group-bys concurrently, then five analyses in parallel goroutines, and prints a formatted terminal briefing with ASCII bars and MemStats telemetry. Builder and Strategy patterns are real, but all analyses live in one 320-line Execute method, there are no tests, every file has a BOM and zero indentation (never gofmt'd), and the README and run.sh are corrupted by a PowerShell paste.
stakeholder_value: The five questions are well chosen and cross-dataset in form (ratios, vacancy cohorts, spatial proximity, district composite, channel equity) with named stakeholders. Their answers are worthless in practice because both inputs are generated by the student's own seeded generator with the effects planted in; e.g. Canton's '55x dumping multiplier' and 4,906 'hazards within 150 m' are artifacts of uniform request allocation and centroid jitter.
issues: Both datasets are synthetic output of internal/seed/generator.go (sequential SR-/VBN- IDs, 16 neighborhoods, impossible address/neighborhood pairs, planted effects) yet README calls them Open Baltimore exports
Generator is the default path: seed.EnsureDatasets runs on every start and regenerates missing files; no fetch/download path
run.sh fails with a bash syntax error (README text + PowerShell @' pasted above the shebang)
README is 9 corrupted CRLF lines with an unterminated code block; no verify instructions
No tests; source not gofmt'd (no indentation, BOM in every file)
Engine.Execute is a single 320-line method; neighborhood profile aggregation is sequential
Output headings oversell the system (e.g. 'Verifying dataset integrity' while generating data)
rationale: Credit is earned for a clean Go build, genuine race-free worker-pool concurrency, Builder/Strategy structure and five cross-dataset questions with ASCII output. The grade collapses on the data requirement (fully simulated data presented as real, generator as default: 0/15), a broken run script and near-empty README, no tests, and results that only reflect planted synthetic effects. 51/100, F.
